result.title: PhysDNet: Physics-Driven Gradient Amplification for Real-Time Image Dehazing
result.comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026. Code, deployment scripts and pre-trained checkpoints: https://github.com/Heatdh/PhysDnet
result.summary: Modern dehazing networks are often computationally expensive and overfit to synthetic haze, limiting real-time deployment. This underscores an urgent demand for efficient, high-fidelity restoration methods that can operate on resource-constrained edge devices in practical, dynamic environments. We introduce PhysDNet, a lightweight multimodal architecture that fuses NIR imagery with sparse LiDAR depth and is trained with a physics-constrained dual-head objective. Differentiating through a fixed Koschmieder inversion induces density-adaptive gradient amplification, acting as an implicit resource allocation mechanism that concentrates learning on heavily degraded regions without increasing inference cost. PhysDNet delivers superior restoration with minimal capacity and enhanced training efficiency, facilitating real-time deployment on edge devices without increasing inference overhead. On the Seeing Through Fog benchmark, PhysDNet outperforms competitors by 1.67 dB at 5.2 times lower compute while recovering 54.9% of fog-induced detection loss. Ablations and cross-domain evaluations show that physics-guided training improves generalization, including under non-homogeneous haze that violates the Koschmieder assumption. PhysDNet further demonstrates compatibility with fixed-function NPUs, running at 29/45/99 FPS at <4 W across L/M/S variants. Code, deployment scripts and pre-trained checkpoints are available at https://github.com/Heatdh/PhysDnet.

AI.brief_summary: 提出轻量多模态去雾网络 PhysDNet，融合 NIR 图像与稀疏 LiDAR 深度，以物理约束双头目标训练；对固定 Koschmieder 逆变换求导得到随雾密度自适应的梯度放大，在不增加推理开销下把学习集中到重退化区域。
AI.relevance_reason: “可微物理逆变换→随退化程度自适应的梯度加权”是一种训练期资源／监督分配机制，或可供核查如何按证据可靠性重加权 latent 状态的训练信号；但论文本身无推理期状态生成，与 LVR 主线联系间接。
